segments.text: I think this is the sutra we have to deal with.
So this process of meditation, which is not beyond Anav-Anav-Upaya, this process of meditation is already explained.
Now the other means of meditations, which are interconnected with the process of this meditation dhana, pranayam, dharna, pratyahar and samadhi.
These are now explained in this next sutra.
Nadi samhar, bhutjay, bhut kayval, bhut prataktani. Nadi samhara means merging of breathing movements.
Bhutjay means attaining control on gross elements.
Control on gross elements is when you suffer, but internally you don't suffer. You are caught by fever, but internally you don't suffer from that pain.
This is called controlling on gross elements. That is bhutjay.
Next is bhut kayval. Taking away mind from gross objects of senses and directing them towards the only breathing movement.
This is bhut kayval. Just divert attention from all objective senses and direct it towards the center of your movements.
This is bhut kayval. And bhut prataktani means carrying away your consciousness from the clutches of elementary field.
Points and you are painful. In leg, you carry away the consciousness of that pain from that leg and you are without pain. You can enjoy.
This is what yoginam bhavini yaniyatisha yogis experience. These powers are experienced by yogis.
Now he explains this sutra thoroughly. Nadi nam, first nadi samhar, what nadi samhar means.
Pranapana, the vahini nam, sushinam, samhara, merging of breathing movements in the central vein, sushamna, that is nadi samhar.
Pranapana yuktya, by maintaining awareness in inhale and exhale, that is pranapana yuktya.
And by that, ekatra udhana vahiniyatvani madhyanadam, vilyanadabhada nam, you direct and carry these movements of breaths in inhale and exhale in the central vein sushamna.
It is said in Srimat Sachhande.
Upasavena means by right nostril. You should take out your breath.
Rajatam means take out breath. Savenaivat puraeth, you should take in by left nostril. Savena means left nostril.
This is the purification of all veins and the purification of the path towards liberation, final liberation.
Upasavena means right nostril. Savena means left.
Rajatam is done in three ways.
Rajatam is one way of pranayama.
Inhaling is another way and the third way is retaining it.
These are these three ways of retaining, retention of breath, pranayama or gross.
And these ways are common or ordinary. Savena means common, common to everybody.
Nobody knows how to do it. Purnacha-bhantarietriya. But there are other three internal ways of this which are uncommon.
Abhantarena-rechaetha, purietha-bhantarena-tu, nispandam, kumbakam-krittva, karya-cha-bhantara-striya.
You have to take out your breath, not to take it exactly. Take out your breath in the center of navel.
Just put it in, put it, put it a bit push in the navel, in the center of navel.
Don't let it go out. This is exhaling, internal exhaling, purietha-bhantarena-tu.
Then you should again take it in the center of navel.
Give it a push first and take it back in navel. Just push and back, push and back.
Only you have not to breathe out or in. This is uncommon way of breathing exercise.
And nispandam, kumbakam-krittva. So this kumbaka means kumbaka here functions in three ways.
While taking out breath, it is already kumbaka. It is not going away.
When you take it in, it is not going away. When you retain it, it is there.
So in the center of navel, you have to do all these three ways of pranayama.
And these three ways of pranayama are done by advanced duties.
This vaya pranayama is uncommon. This is what is explained in Nadi Sanghara first.
Then next comes bhutjaaya. Now he explains bhutjaaya.
Bhutanaam pratyadinam jayodarana-bir vasi-kara. Just to attain control on these five elements
from earth to ether by contemplation. Dharana-bir vasi-kara. Just to control it.
Yatoktam-tatrava, this is already said in satsandha.
Why we dharana-guste aagne-i nabi-madhata. Whenever you want to control the wind in your body,
you must put dharana, you must put contemplation, contemplative mood awareness.
On the left foot, left toe of foot, left big toe, biggest toe.
It is done by left toe. On the left toe, yes, toe of foot.
This dharana is concerned with vaya, wind. When there is wind trouble in your body,
by vaya dharana, you can remove it. Rumatic pain or something like that.
This dharana will help it, not help it, remove it totally. All the rumatic pain is removed by this dharana.
Aagne-i nabi-madhata, when there is insufficient element of fire in your body,
less fire, less warmth in your body, you should put, you should meditate in the center of navel.
Aagne-i nabi-madhata in the center of navel, navel means navel.
Mahayi-kantide-shetu. And there is lessening of flesh in your body.
Then to increase that flesh in your body, you have to put dharana on earth.
And that dharana is concerned in the pit of throat.
Mahayi-pratvaya. Mahayi-kantide-shetu. In this throat pit, you have to concentrate.
Then your flesh will rise in your body. Varuni-gantikashita, when there is less water or you are flooded,
you are going to drown in ocean. There you must put Varuni dharana, contemplate on gel, water.
And that contemplation is done at the place of Gantika. Gantika means it is just near Thalu,
near that small piece hanging in throat. That is Gantika, huh?
Inner tongue. Inner tongue. There you have to contemplate and Varuni will come in existence.
Aakashidharana murdhni sarvasiddhikari swata. Aakashidharana, dharana on ether is done on head, murda.
It gives you all powers. This dharana will lead you to all powers, which are desired.
This is Bhuta-jai. Now third, Bhuta-kaivalyam. Bhuta-dya-kaivalyam. What is Bhuta-dya-kaivalyam?
You have to remove, you have to get rid of Bhuta's. How? Chittasya-tata-pratyaharanam.
Drawing back, pratyaharanam means drawing back. You should withdraw your mind from objective pleasures.
And direct your mind in the center of breath. Just concentrate on the center of breath and draw your attention,
which is gone in object of field, object of pleasures. This is said in satsanda.
Direct your consciousness in the center of navel. And direct your mind also in that center.
Manashtra-indray-ghojara, carrying it away from the organs of senses.
This pranayama is fourth pranayama, and it is appeased way of retention.
You have not to breathe out and in there. This is what is already explained to you. Just now.
Radhyat-nabhav pranasya-vishya-bhya-manasascha-tatrava-sancharana.
From heart, you should direct your heart to the center of navel.
And direct all your objective pleasures to your mind. No, direct your mind, which is gone in object of pleasures.
Direct your mind towards the center of navel.
Now, both pratakthani is the last one.
Just to carry away your consciousness from gross elements.
What is that? Tata-anuparat-sachhanda-chidat-mata. When one's consciousness is not influenced,
Anuparat means not influenced by elementary field.
This is said in sachhanda.
Bittak remain sarvani-unmanantani-yanica, purvokta-laksana-yadevi-tyakta-sachhanda-tama-ra-jade.
When all these gross five elements are subsided, the force of all these gross elements is subsided.
Up to the stage of unmana, beyond samana.
Then by doing this, you become just like Lord Shiva. You become one with Shiva.
This way in this sutra, naadi-samhar-bhut-jai-bhut-kevel-bhut-pratakthani,
in other words, it is said in sambhopaya also.
In bhut-sandana-bhut-pratakthavisya-sangata, this is sutra in sambhopaya.
In the first awakening of sutras, bhut-sandana-bhut-pratakthavisya-sangata,
in this sutra also you get the same sense. But why he has repeated this sutra again here in Anupaya?
In Anupaya he has repeated the same what is already explained in sambhopaya,
the first awakening of sutras.
The difference is, sambhopaya is samaavistasya ayatranthobavati.
The one who is established in sambhopaya, in the trance of samaavisya,
to him these powers come automatically without any effort, without putting any effort on it.
But to this sadhaka of Anupaya, these powers come after putting effort on them to achieve.
